question: Ukraine is pushing for the conclusion of a status agreement with the EU to make it possible for Frontex operations to take place on its territory. Such an agreement would allow for armed border surveillance activities and operations to counter cross-border crime similar to those already being carried out in other third countries. Discussions are already under way in the relevant EU bodies. 1.
When does the Council intend to take a decision as regards the mandate for negotiations for a status agreement with Ukraine, and where has this been or is currently being discussed?

In the Council’s view, what is the added value of such an agreement compared with the cooperation already in place, particularly bearing in mind the support already being provided by Frontex and the European Union Advisory Mission for Civilian Security Sector Reform Ukraine?
Have there been any meetings or discussions with the Ukrainian Government on a potential status agreement, and if so, what was discussed?
answer: When adopting a decision on authorising the opening of negotiations, the Council acts on the basis of a recommendation submitted by the Commission. The Commission has not submitted any recommendation to the Council on authorising the opening of negotiations on a status agreement on operational activities by the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) in Ukraine.

European Union Advisory Mission (EUAM) Ukraine is mandated to provide strategic advice, mentoring and training for the reform of Ukraine’s integrated border management (IBM), including on maritime aspects, contributing to combating border-management-related corruption, organised crime and transnational crime, and all forms of smuggling.

The mission and Frontex agreed a working arrangement on 19 February 2024, allowing for their closer cooperation in the field of border security and integrated border management in Ukraine. The Council has not held any discussions with the Ukrainian government on a potential status agreement between the European Union and Ukraine.
